title: Journey - Five Days of Gratitude - Day 4: A grateful word

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, a soft smile in the voice, unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Five Days of Gratitude. <short pause> This is day four, A Grateful Word. <short pause> We have been giving thanks to God. You are good. This is from You. Even here. <short pause> Today, that thanks is going to find its way out of your mouth... and toward a person.

Let's get comfortable first. <short pause> Soften your face, and the place between your eyes. <short pause> Let your tongue rest. It does so much work. <short pause> Take an easy breath... <short pause> and for a moment, there is nothing you need to say to anyone.

So much of our gratitude never gets delivered. <short pause> We feel it. We mean it. <short pause> We think, I must tell her one day what that meant to me. <short pause> And then the day fills up. <short pause> Somewhere, there are people who changed our lives... who have no idea that they did.

Paul was in prison when he wrote to the church in Colossae. <short pause> He couldn't visit them, or put a hand on anyone's shoulder. <short pause> Words were what he had. <short pause> And this is what he asked them to do with theirs, in chapter three, verse seventeen.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
parts.text: And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: In word or deed. <short pause> So thanks is not only a feeling that happens inside us. <short pause> It has a voice, and it has hands. <short pause> And when you thank a person for their kindness, you are not taking anything away from God. <short pause> Very often... that person is how His kindness got to you.

parts.style: gently wondering, slow, leaving room to answer
parts.text: Who comes to mind? <short pause> It may be someone from this week, who did a small thing well. <short pause> It may be someone from long ago. <short pause> A teacher. A neighbor. A grandmother. <short pause> The friend who didn't give advice. <short pause> The stranger who was gentle on a terrible day. <short pause> Let one face step forward... only one.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Now we'll build one sentence for them, in three pieces. <short pause> First... when you. <short pause> Name exactly what they did. Not, you're so nice. <short pause> When you drove me home. When you remembered his name. <short pause> Finish that piece in your heart.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: The second piece... it helped me. <short pause> Tell them what it did. <short pause> It helped me feel less alone. It helped me keep going. <short pause> And then the last piece, which needs nothing added to it at all... <short pause> thank you. <short pause> Put the three together now, and hear yourself say it to them.

parts.style: warm reassurance, slow, resting between sentences
parts.text: If that person has died, or it wouldn't be wise or safe to contact them, your sentence is not wasted. <short pause> Say it to God instead. <short pause> He knows how to keep a thank you. <short pause> And if you feel shy, that's all right. <short pause> A grateful word can be clumsy, and still be one of the best things someone hears all year.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Here is our fourth sentence, for all the people His goodness has traveled through. <short pause> Say it with the others. <short pause> You are good. <short pause> This is from You. <short pause> Even here. <short pause> Through them.

Let's pray. <short pause> God and Father, thank You for the one whose face I have just seen. <short pause> Thank You for loving me through their hands, and their time, and their words. <short pause> Give me the courage to tell them. <short pause> And make me, for somebody, a way that Your kindness arrives. <short pause> In the name of the Lord Jesus. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: soft, warm, slow sending, resting between phrases
parts.text: Your practice for today is to deliver it. <short pause> A message, a note, a call, or a word as you pass. <short pause> Don't polish it. <short pause> When you... it helped me... thank you. <short pause> Send it before it has time to become one day. <short pause> Go kindly.
